content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper extends the idea of classifier guidance for generating class-conditioned samples from diffusion model to compositional generation with a pretrained generative model. Specifically, it first trains a diffusion model on the latent space and a latent classifier, then it generates samples from the latent diffusion model using the guidance of the classifier, where the composition comes from composing the gradient of the classifier corresponding to several attributes.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

1. The idea of using classifier guidance for compositional generation is interesting. Classifier guidance has shown promising results for conditional sampling from diffusion models, and this work makes a novel exploration on composing the classifier gradients of different classes.

2. The method is clearly presented and easy to understand.

Weakness:

1. Some claims are not justified. For example, you claim that compared to Nie et al, your method is latent space agnostic and can be applied to any latent variable model. However, there is no justification on this argument. Why is your method latent space agnostic? What latent variable model does not work for Nie et al.? My understanding is that Nie et al requires a reparameterization trick which may require a prior on latent variables, so that it might not work on deterministic latent variable model such as auto-encoder. However, your method requires training a latent diffusion model, which corresponds to build a prior for latent variables, and the same idea can be added to Nie et al as well. I think there should not be difference in applicability. You should elaborate this point clearly.

2. Not clear advantage in results. First of all, in Figure 1, compared to Nie et al., clearly your samples does not follow the attribute 55 y/o. Many of your generated faces look young, while Nie et al seems to align with this condition better. Secondly, the FID score in table 1 does not show clear advantages over baselines. 

3. The purpose of section 2.3 is not clear. Lemma 1 is just the loss derivation of diffusion models, and I do not see why Lemma 2 is important there. Since the title is " MODEL TRAINING", I suggest introducing the training pipeline.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The writing quality is good, and the method is presented clearly. The novelty is a bit limited, as it is an extension of classifier guidance, but I still value the novelty of this work. Since the experiments are based on pre-trained models, and the training of unconditional diffusion models is straightforward, it shouldn't be hard to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: As stated above, although it is an interesting idea, I have some concerns on the experimental results and lack of justification of some arguments. Therefore I think this submission is slightly below the threshold.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

display_title: Official Review of Paper3838 by Reviewer Pegm

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposed a new method that trains a latent diffusion model and latent classifiers to perform classifier guidance in the latent space of pre-trained generative models for compositional generation and manipulation. They claimed that their method is model-agnostic and space-agnostic. Besides, they showed that when the pre-trained models have a disentangled latent space, simply applying linear classifiers (i.e., vector arithmetic in the latent space) is sufficient to perform competitively with previous methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- This work is clearly written, and the presentations of the proposed idea and experiment settings are overall very easy to follow. 
- It is good to see the systematic study of the compositional generation in the context of latent diffusion models and classifier guidance. In particular, the idea of developing a model-agnostic and space-agnostic method for compositional generation is interesting and useful.
- Experiments show comparable compositional generation results compared with LACE in synthetic image generation and editing, and better performance in real image editing.

Weaknesses:
- The idea of training a latent diffusion model and then applying a guidance to a latent diffusion model is not completely new. For example, LDM (or stable diffusion) actually used the same idea to add text-based control in their latent diffusion model. Although I understand the difference between conditioning on texts and attributes, I think it is still reasonable to consider them as very similar approaches.
- This work argued that in the latent space, it is more intuitive to perform classifier guidance than classifier-free guidance, but there is no experimental evidence to support this claim. We know that LDM used classifier-free guidance in their latent diffusion model and it worked pretty well.
- I’m not sure if building a connection between applying a linear classifier and a vector arithmetic in the latent space is something new. Intuitively, it is straightforward to see that the direction vector discovered by a linear classifier corresponds to an editing direction in the latent space. Also, in the proof of Lemma 3, I’m not sure if the assumptions make sense in practice. For instance, why can we assume $p(z_t)$ is a non-informative distribution? What does it mean by “the reverse process latent diffusion model converges at $t=0$”? Does $\alpha_0^i$ also depend on $z_0$? I hope the authors can take these questions into consideration and make this part more clear. 
- In figures and tables, it is better to explicitly explain what “Ours-linear” and “Ours-Diffusion” mean, respectively. Also, if I understand correctly, “Ours-Diffusion” refers to the nonlinear version of the proposed method. It is confusing to me because, I think, the method “Ours-linear” also has a latent diffusion model in the first place, and the only difference is whether we use linear or nonlinear classifiers.
- I think it is incorrect to say “$W+$ space is a concatenation of 18 different 512-dimensional $w$ vectors in StyleGAN2. First, only when the output image resolution is 1024, it contains 18 $w$ vectors. Second, the “$W+$ space in the original StyleGAN (res=1024) contains the same 18 $w$ vectors.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: I’m satisfied with the overall writing quality and originality of the work. I raised some concerns about the clarity and the significance in the weaknesses above. I think the work provided sufficient details for reproducing the main results.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I have major concerns about some claims in the work and the significance of the proposed method.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper discusses compositional image generation and manipulation with diffusion models in the latent space. The idea is to use classifier guidance on the latent space (Liu et al. 2022). Empirical results are shown over compositional image generation and image manipulation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- Experiment results seems to outperform or at least competitive against methods on the latent space based on Langevin dynamics or ODEs.
- The method works on "encoder-less" architectures such as GANs.

Weakness:
- Lack of technical depth: the idea is simply applying compositional generation on image-based diffusion models to latent-based diffusion models. In the method section, none of 2.1, 2.2, or 2.3 are originally proposed in this paper. 

- Lack of discussion of important related work: the idea is quite similar to an earlier work [1], which also trained a latent diffusion model and showed conditional generation and image manipulation results using linear classifiers. [1] is used in Diffusion Autoencoders for comparison, so it would be natural to consider the sampling approach from [1] as a baseline.

- The compositions assume that the labels are independent given latent, but this assumption is not necessarily always correct. As a result, the method does not necessarily work well with non-independent conditions. 

[1] D2C: Diffusion-Denoising Models for Few-shot Conditional Generation, NeurIPS 21.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity (Fair): the method itself is not hard to understand, but many of the components in the method section would be better suited to fall under a "background" section with clear citations attributing the original authors of the ideas.

Quality (Fair): The method section are generally clear, except for not having an explicit algorithm for manipulation. Also, for a reader not familiar with the literature, it is possible to not know the connection between diffusion models and scores, so the gap between 2.1 and 2.2 is quite large. For experiments, the compositional generation and image manipulation lack a lot of qualitative results. It would be natural to include qualitative results (in the appendix) to see how the method works in practice. 

Originality (Fair): as mentioned earlier, the method combines several existing techniques and is very similar to the earlier D2C work.

Reproducibility: while code is not provided, I think the method should generally be reproducible, but it could help to give a more detailed descriptions of the method end-to-end.
content.summary_of_the_review: While there are some interesting empirical results, there seems to be a lack of technical novelty, which mostly seems like compositing (relatively straightforward) ideas from other papers.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a method based on latent diffusion models to generate composable editing of real and synthetic samples. Specifically, classifiers are trained on latent features to be used for classifier-guidance of latent diffusion models. Experiments are performed on a StyleGAN2 and a diffusion autoencoder.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Although composable and controllable image generation is certainly an interesting topic, the results in this paper are not sufficient for conference acceptance because the experiments performed are sparse and limited, and only a few manipulations of facial features are shown. No independent control over features is shown (although this is touted as an advantage of "disentangled latent space" (p.3)).  In addition, although it is briefly mentioned, that there is no comparison to _classifier-free_ guidance; this would be essential as it is a far simpler method (and could be competitive and easy to implement). If there is a reason for this, it should be discussed. 

Below are some thoughts that came to me while reading the paper: 
- Fig. 1 + 2 would work best if only individual features were changed --> Is the announced "disentanglement" property valid, i.e., can we control only certain features like "smile"?
- There is way too much mathematical notation for very little content. Section 2.4 is unnecessary in my opinion and could either be removed or moved to the appendix. $\nabla_{z_t}   p(z_t) = 0$ is a very strong assumption and does not hold for typical diffusion processes where data is  gradually diffused. 
- Classifiers are trained only on clean latent data $z$. How much worse is this than training time-dependent classifiers? This should be evaluated.
- P.3: _"Another advantage is the ability to use different guidance techniques in the
latent space, since training latent guidance terms is typically easier than training other manipulation methods.
Manipulation methods in image space"_ --> Why is this generally true? What latent spaces are we referring to here? Note that certain latent spaces may be invariant to certain input features.
- P.3: _"One of the advantages of modeling the latent space instead of the image space
is that the latent space has some properties that the image space does not, such as disentanglement
(Bengio et al., 2013)."_ --> Under what circumstances does a latent space provide "disentanglement". What exactly are the properties associated with it?
- P.5: What is the "pushforward" distribution?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written; the methods should be reproducible. As discussed above, quality and novelty are lacking.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the general topic and idea of using diffusion models and additive properties in the score function space for composable generation of images, the paper fails to deliver an convincing argument for the proposed approach based on classifier-guidance. See "weaknesses" above.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
